title: The $67 million behind six Senate races, and what it bought
dek: A crypto super PAC was the biggest outside spender in The Watch's federal data, and most of its money went into an Alabama primary. The filings so far show only part of what the national players spent.

states.name: Alaska
states.title: In Alaska, a $31.6 Million Senate Air War Ends Almost Even
states.dek: Outside groups split Alaska's Senate spending almost down the middle, but Mary Peltola's campaign outraised Dan Sullivan's by more than two and a half to one. She leads narrowly in an uncalled race. The Democrat for governor, who had far more outside money behind him, leads by a wide margin.
states.summary: Outside Senate money split almost evenly; Peltola, who raised $36.9M, leads narrowly in an uncalled race.

states.name: Alabama
states.title: Crypto Money Carried Barry Moore Through Alabama's Senate Primary
states.dek: A crypto industry super PAC spent $12.2 million for Barry Moore before the June runoff, and no outside group spent for his Democratic opponent. In the governor's race, Tommy Tuberville outraised Doug Jones by about $11 million.
states.summary: Outside groups spent $22.6 million on Alabama's Senate race, nearly all in the GOP primary; Barry Moore and Tommy Tuberville won.

states.name: Arkansas
states.title: Cotton-linked super PAC spent millions defining Shoffner; Cotton won by 12
states.dek: Outside money in Arkansas's Senate race went almost entirely to one side, mostly through a super PAC run by Sen. Tom Cotton's allies. Cotton won easily, but his margin was far below Donald Trump's in 2024.
states.summary: A Cotton-allied super PAC spent about $3.9 million against Hallie Shoffner; Cotton won by 11.9 points, far below Trump's 2024 margin.

states.name: Arizona
states.title: In Arizona, Hobbs and Democrats outspent Turning Point's $18 million Biggs bet
states.dek: Gov. Katie Hobbs and a county Democratic committee funded by the Democratic Governors Association spent far more than Andy Biggs. That gap held even after Turning Point put more than $18 million behind Biggs. Hobbs won by 13 points.
states.summary: Hobbs, her campaign and Democratic party money outspent Biggs and Turning Point by a wide margin; she won by 13 points.

states.name: California
states.title: California's record-cost governor's race: labor, Realtors and a tribe backed Becerra
states.dek: Most of the record $350 million in ads ran before the June primary. Xavier Becerra and the committees backing him outspent Steve Hilton, who relied on small donors and AI-made ads. Becerra won by 30 points.
states.summary: Becerra and allied committees funded by labor, Realtors and a tribe outspent Hilton and won by 30 points in a record race.

states.name: Colorado
states.title: Colorado's biggest money fight came in June, and the bigger spender lost
states.dek: A super PAC funded by Michael Bloomberg spent about $11 million to make Michael Bennet governor, and Phil Weiser beat him. In the Senate race, the FEC shows only $800,000 in outside money, all of it spent on the Democratic side.
states.summary: Colorado's outside money went mostly into June primaries; a super PAC funded by Bloomberg lost, and November drew little.

states.name: Connecticut
states.title: Lamont's own millions met Fazio's public grant, and outside money stayed home
states.dek: Gov. Ned Lamont spent $18.7 million through Oct. 27, nearly all of it his own money. Republican Ryan Fazio spent $17 million from Connecticut's public-financing grant. National groups that spent millions here in 2022 stayed out. Lamont won by 19 points.
states.summary: Self-funded Lamont and publicly financed Fazio spent about equally; super PACs stayed out, and Lamont won a third term by 19 points.

states.name: Delaware
states.title: In Delaware, the money skipped the Senate race and went down the ballot
states.dek: Chris Coons outraised his Republican challenger about 40 to 1 and won easily. Delaware's hardest-fought spending came in September's Democratic primaries, where corporate law firms and national groups paid for ads in races for treasurer and the legislature.
states.summary: Coons won easily; law firms and national PACs paid for the ads in Delaware's down-ballot Democratic primaries, with mixed results.

states.name: Florida
states.title: Ken Griffin's money backed both Florida Republicans who narrowly held on
states.dek: Republicans spent far more than Democrats in Florida's Senate and governor's races. A super PAC backed by Ken Griffin ran most of the outside ads in the Senate race. Both Republicans won by less than three points.
states.summary: Florida Republicans far outspent Democrats and won both statewide races, but each by less than three points.

states.name: Georgia
states.title: Georgia's $200 million self-funder lost; Ossoff's 13-to-1 money edge held
states.dek: Rick Jackson's own fortune paid for much of Georgia's record ad spending, and he still lost the governor's race by nearly nine points. Jon Ossoff raised almost 13 times as much as Mike Collins and won by 18.
states.summary: Georgia: Jackson's self-funded ads lost to Bottoms; Ossoff, far outraising Collins and helped by more outside money, won by 18.

states.name: Hawaii
states.title: Hawaii's Green outraised Cordery nine to one, then won by a record
states.dek: No national group spent money on Hawaii's race for governor. Gov. Josh Green's $3.9 million campaign, along with a carpenters-funded super PAC that backed his running mate, far outspent a Republican campaign that raised $430,800. The Democrats won by 45 points.
states.summary: Hawaii: Gov. Josh Green raised $3.9 million to Gary Cordery's $430,800 and won by 45 points, a state record.

states.name: Iowa
states.title: Iowa's record money fight ends with Democrats winning Senate and governor
states.dek: Republican super PACs and national party groups spent heavily to keep an open Senate seat and the governor's office. Democrats Josh Turek and Rob Sand raised more than their opponents and won both races, by 4.1 and 11 points.
states.summary: Turek and Sand outraised their rivals in Iowa's costly top races while GOP groups poured in late money; Democrats won both.

states.name: Idaho
states.title: Idaho's incumbents outspent their challengers and won, by narrower margins than Trump
states.dek: Jim Risch and Brad Little had far more money than their opponents and both won easily. Very little outside money came in, and the largest late Democratic ad buy was for an abortion-rights measure that failed.
states.summary: Idaho: Risch and Little outspent challengers several times over and won by more than 20 points; abortion-rights ad money went through Pickens.

states.name: Illinois
states.title: In Illinois, Pritzker's $90.5 Million Ran Into Almost No Opposing Ads
states.dek: Gov. JB Pritzker put $90.5 million of his own money into a rematch with Darren Bailey, whose 2022 megadonor dropped out. Pritzker won by 23.5 points. Juliana Stratton won the Senate race by slightly more, with no outside money.
states.summary: Pritzker self-funded $90.5 million and outspent Bailey 25-to-1; he won by 23.5 points, Stratton by 24.3 without outside money.

states.name: Kansas
states.title: Kansas Republicans Outspent Democrats for Governor; Democrats Outspent Them for Senate
states.dek: National Republican groups spent more than twice what Democrats did on the governor's race, which is still uncalled. In the Senate race, which set a Kansas spending record, Democrats spent more and their candidate won.
states.summary: Kansas: Democrats outspent Republicans and won the Senate seat; Republicans outspent Democrats for governor, where the Democrat leads but no winner has been called.

states.name: Kentucky
states.title: Kentucky's Senate money was spent on the May primary, not November
states.dek: Billionaires, crypto firms and groups that don't name their donors spent tens of millions to choose Mitch McConnell's successor before May. Andy Barr won the seat by 12 points, after a general election in which only one side bought much advertising.
states.summary: Kentucky: Most of the Senate money went into the GOP primary; Andy Barr then beat Charles Booker by 12 points.

states.name: Louisiana
states.title: Landry-tied super PAC backed Letlow; Davis, with little outside help, nearly won
states.dek: Most of the outside money in Louisiana's Senate race was spent in the spring, when Julia Letlow ousted Sen. Bill Cassidy. In the fall, Republicans spent late, Democrats barely at all, and Letlow won by 1.8 points.
states.summary: Louisiana: pro-Letlow super PACs outspent Davis's side in the fall; she won the Senate seat by 1.8 points, 25,857 votes.

states.name: Massachusetts
states.title: Minogue's record $19.5 million doesn't dent Healey's Massachusetts margin
states.dek: A Republican executive paid for most of his own campaign and set the state's spending records. A Democratic governors' super PAC and a friend's super PAC also spent money. Gov. Maura Healey still won by 27 points.
states.summary: Massachusetts: Mike Minogue spent a record $19.5 million of his own money and lost to Maura Healey by 27 points.

states.name: Maryland
states.title: Moore Outspent Cox Many Times Over, Then Spent Late on Redistricting
states.dek: Gov. Wes Moore had about 48 times Dan Cox's cash heading into the fall. He won a second term easily and spent his closing ad money on Question 3, which passed even though polls had shown it losing.
states.summary: Moore outraised Cox many times over, won by 31.5 points, and moved late ad money to a redistricting measure that passed.

states.name: Maine
states.title: In Maine, the bigger spender won the governor's race and lost the Senate race
states.dek: Republican groups put well over $100 million into ads to save Susan Collins, and she lost. In the governor's race, a group tied to the Democratic Governors Association had the airwaves almost to itself.
states.summary: Republican outside groups spent the most defending Susan Collins and lost; Democrats spent the most on the governor's race and won.

states.name: Michigan
states.title: In Michigan, the bigger spender won one race and lost the other
states.dek: Jocelyn Benson's allies far outspent John James in the governor's race. Republicans outspent Abdul El-Sayed in the record Senate race. Democrats won both, by margins far wider than Michigan's 2024 presidential vote.
states.summary: Michigan: Benson's side outspent James and won. Rogers's side outspent El-Sayed and lost. Democrats won both by wide margins.

states.name: Minnesota
states.title: Uihlein money evened Minnesota's governor race; Klobuchar won by nearly 13 points
states.dek: A super PAC funded almost entirely by the Uihlein family spent more than $14 million to help Lisa Demuth and attack Amy Klobuchar. Klobuchar won by more than Kamala Harris's 2024 margin. The Senate race got far less outside money.
states.summary: In Minnesota, Uihlein-funded Restore Sanity outspent Demuth's own campaign about fourfold; Klobuchar still won the governorship by 12.8 points.

states.name: Mississippi
states.title: Viral beef ad, late PAC money put Mississippi's Senate seat in doubt
states.dek: Democratic super PACs and the party's Senate committee came in late. In the final stretch, AdImpact data showed Cindy Hyde-Smith outgunned on the air. Scott Colom leads by 2,574 votes, and the Associated Press has not called the race.
states.summary: Late Democratic super PAC money followed a viral ad. Scott Colom leads Cindy Hyde-Smith by 2,574 votes in a race that is still uncalled.

states.name: Montana
states.title: In Montana, Bodnar's backers outspent Alme's. Alme won by 10 points.
states.dek: Independent Seth Bodnar and the super PACs behind him outspent Republican Kurt Alme's side in Montana's open Senate race, according to counts drawn from FEC filings. Alme still won by about 51,000 votes in a three-way race.
states.summary: Pro-Bodnar groups outspent Alme's allies, but Republican Kurt Alme won Montana's open Senate seat by 10.6 points.

states.name: North Carolina
states.title: Republicans led North Carolina's Senate ad spending, then pulled out as Cooper won
states.dek: The Senate Leadership Fund promised $71 million to elect Michael Whatley and stopped at about $30 million. Roy Cooper's campaign raised more than three times Whatley's total and won by nearly 20 points.
states.summary: North Carolina: Republican super PACs outspent Democrats on summer ads, then left; Cooper, the bigger fundraiser, won by 19.6 points.

states.name: Nebraska
states.title: Nebraska's Senate fight drew about $55 million in outside money, and Ricketts held on
states.dek: A crypto super PAC, a group tied to Senate Republicans and a Democratic-funded PAC behind ads about pardons spent tens of millions on Pete Ricketts and Dan Osborn. In the governor's race, the Republican Governors Association backed Jim Pillen.
states.summary: Outside groups spent heavily on both sides in Nebraska; Ricketts won by 6 points and Pillen by 8.

states.name: New Hampshire
states.title: In New Hampshire, Ayotte's money edge held; Sununu's outside help didn't
states.dek: Gov. Kelly Ayotte raised about five times as much as Cinde Warmington and won by four points while Democrats won down the ballot. In the Senate race, Republican groups outspent Democratic ones, and Chris Pappas won by nearly 14.
states.summary: Ayotte outraised her rival five to one and won; heavy Republican outside spending didn't win Sununu the Senate seat.

states.name: New Jersey
states.title: In New Jersey, Republicans outspent Democrats for Tom Kean Jr. and lost
states.dek: Most of the outside money in New Jersey went to one House district, the 7th. A House Republican super PAC paid for TV ads through another committee, then pulled out. In South Jersey, a late Democratic ad buy came before an upset.
states.summary: In New Jersey's 7th District, Republican groups outspent Democrats but Rep. Tom Kean Jr. lost; Cory Booker won easily.

states.name: New Mexico
states.title: Haaland Outspent Hull More Than Seven to One in New Mexico
states.dek: Deb Haaland's record campaign fund and a $2.5 million ad push by a Democratic Governors Association-backed committee faced no reported Republican outside group. She won by 14.7 points. The state's Senate race swung harder with little outside money.
states.summary: Haaland outspent Hull more than seven to one, a DGA-funded PAC added $2.5 million in ads, and she won by 14.7 points.

states.name: Nevada
states.title: Nevada's GOP ad edge of $32.6 million didn't save Lombardo
states.dek: Gov. Joe Lombardo's campaign and allied PACs, funded heavily by the Republican Governors Association and Budget Suites owner Robert Bigelow, spent far more on ads than the other side. Attorney General Aaron Ford still won by 7.7 points.
states.summary: Nevada: Republicans outspent Democrats about $2.47 to $1 on governor ads; Democrat Aaron Ford still beat Gov. Joe Lombardo by 7.7 points.

states.name: New York
states.title: Uber and Dolan money poured into New York's lopsided governor's race
states.dek: Gov. Kathy Hochul beat Bruce Blakeman by nearly 20 points. She had far more money, both in her campaign and in outside groups, while the money for Blakeman came largely from businesses linked to James Dolan.
states.summary: Hochul and her allies, led by Uber, outspent Blakeman and his Dolan-funded allies and won by nearly 20 points.

states.name: Ohio
states.title: Ohio Republicans outspent Democrats on ads and lost both top races
states.dek: Crypto PACs, a billionaire candidate's loans and a $10 million check from a Pennsylvania investor helped Republicans outspend Democrats in Ohio's Senate and governor's races. Sherrod Brown and Amy Acton won anyway, by wide margins.
states.summary: Republicans and their allies outspent Democrats on Ohio ads, but Sherrod Brown and Amy Acton won the Senate and governor's races.

states.name: Oklahoma
states.title: Mazzei's $12.8 million in loans and RGA ads held Oklahoma's governorship
states.dek: The Republican nominee paid for most of his own campaign, and a Washington-based PAC tied to the Republican Governors Association did most of the outside spending. He won by six points in a state Trump carried by 34.
states.summary: Oklahoma: Mazzei's self-funding and $3 million from Republican governors' allies outspent Munson; he won by six, far below Trump's margin.

states.name: Oregon
states.title: Oregon's last no-limits governor race: $40 million and a familiar winner
states.dek: Christine Drazan and Gov. Tina Kotek raised more than $40 million before Oregon's new contribution limits take effect. Late national money and union checks paid for a TV fight over Trump, abortion and taxes. Kotek won by 9.6 points.
states.summary: Kotek beat Drazan by 9.6 points in a $40 million rematch; Merkley outraised his opponent 28-to-1 and won easily.

states.name: Pennsylvania
states.title: Pennsylvania: Shapiro's nearly $70 million campaign swamps Garrity's late skill-games cash
states.dek: Gov. Josh Shapiro raised about six times what Stacy Garrity did and had the airwaves to himself for months. Skill-games money paid for her ads in the last weeks. Shapiro won by 22 points.
states.summary: Shapiro outraised Garrity about six to one, dominated TV for months and won by 22 points; skill-games donors funded her late ads.

states.name: Rhode Island
states.title: Foulkes outspent a sitting governor, then an independent, and won both races
states.dek: Helena Foulkes spent about $6.8 million and got help from her party, unions and a clean-energy super PAC. That was more than all of her opponents combined. She beat Gov. Dan McKee by 24 points and independent Ken Block by 30.
states.summary: In Rhode Island the money went into the governor's race, and the biggest spender, Democrat Helena Foulkes, won the primary and the general.

states.name: South Carolina
states.title: South Carolina: Outside Money Backed Graham, Andrews Won; Wilson Outspent Johnson
states.dek: Super PACs tied to Senate Republicans, to Lindsey Graham's political network and to the data-center industry spent heavily for Sen. Darline Graham, who lost. In the governor's race, Alan Wilson outspent Jermaine Johnson about two to one and won.
states.summary: Outside groups spent heavily for Darline Graham, who lost; Alan Wilson outspent Jermaine Johnson roughly two to one and won governor.

states.name: South Dakota
states.title: Nearly $10 million on South Dakota's Senate race; Rounds wins by 21
states.dek: Out-of-state super PACs spent millions for and against Sen. Mike Rounds, who beat independent Brian Bengs by a smaller margin than Trump's in 2024. Gov. Larry Rhoden outspent his Democratic challenger about 18 to 1.
states.summary: Super PACs poured millions into the Rounds-Bengs Senate race; Rounds won by 21, and Gov. Larry Rhoden won by 27.

states.name: Tennessee
states.title: In Tennessee, $10 million went after the independent, and Blackburn barely won
states.dek: Committees backing Marsha Blackburn spent close to $10 million attacking David Hatley, a self-funded independent. Blackburn then beat Democrat Jerri Green by 2.5 points, even though Green's campaign could barely afford TV ads.
states.summary: Pro-Blackburn PACs spent about $10 million against an independent, and Blackburn beat an underfunded Democrat by 2.5 points.

states.name: Texas
states.title: Texas: Musk's $224 million and Abbott's $281 million lost to Democrats
states.dek: Republicans and one billionaire outspent Democrats about two to one in Texas's Senate race and eight to one for governor, according to filings and ad trackers. James Talarico and Gina Hinojosa won anyway, by 12 and 7 points.
states.summary: Elon Musk's money helped Texas Republicans far outspend Democrats in the Senate and governor races, and both Democrats won comfortably.

states.name: Virginia
states.title: Warner won Virginia by 22 points with almost no outside money
states.dek: Sen. Mark Warner outraised his Republican challenger about 25 to 1 and faced no outside attack. Virginia's real spending came in an $83 million redistricting vote a court voided, and in Hampton Roads House races where heavier spenders didn't always win.
states.summary: Warner won by 22.7 points on his own $27.5 million; Virginia's big money went to a voided redistricting vote and House races.

states.name: Vermont
states.title: National Republicans' $950,000 ad push backed Phil Scott's sixth Vermont win
states.dek: Amanda Janoo outraised Gov. Phil Scott with small donors and no corporate money. A Republican Governors Association super PAC offset her edge with TV and online ads calling her inexperienced, and Scott won by 6.6 points.
states.summary: An RGA-funded super PAC spent nearly $1 million attacking Amanda Janoo; Phil Scott, outraised, won a sixth term by 6.6 points.

states.name: Wisconsin
states.title: Wisconsin's record governor's race: GOP outspent Democrats nearly 2-to-1 and lost
states.dek: Three billionaires sent tens of millions through the Republican Party of Wisconsin to Tom Tiffany, and a PAC funded by Dick Uihlein added nearly $20 million more. David Crowley was outspent nearly two to one and won by eight points.
states.summary: Wisconsin: Republicans spent $123.6 million, nearly double Democrats, on the governor's race; Democrat David Crowley still won by eight points.

states.name: West Virginia
states.title: West Virginia: Capito's cash edge was vast, but her winning margin halved
states.dek: Sen. Shelley Moore Capito and two super PACs, one tied to AI-industry investors, heavily outspent Democrat Rachel Fetty Anderson. Capito won a third term by 20 points. That is less than half her 2020 margin.
states.summary: Capito, backed by AIPAC-routed donations and two pro-Capito super PACs, beat a barely funded Democrat by 20 points.

states.name: Wyoming
states.title: In Wyoming, a $1.45 Million Primary Attack Failed to Stop Eric Barlow
states.dek: Wyoming's biggest outside spender was a state PAC funded through a committee tied to Harriet Hageman, and it tried to stop Eric Barlow in the governor's primary. He won anyway. Hageman spent about 70 times as much as her Senate opponent.
states.summary: Wyoming: a Hageman-linked PAC spent $1.45 million and couldn't stop Barlow; Hageman outspent Byrd about 70-1 and won.
